topic: Rest days on a multi-day bikepacking trip: when to schedule them and how to use them (laundry, resupply, bike check, sleep). Calm, practical on-screen text; light product mention only.

content.hook: When should you take a bikepacking rest day?

slides.title: When should you take a *rest day*?
slides.body: Bikepacking rest days: when to plan them and how to use them.

slides.title: *When:* every 5–7 riding days
slides.body: Or after a big climb. Pick a town with shops, so the day is useful.

slides.title: *Use it:* sleep, wash, resupply, check
slides.body: Laundry, food shop, bike check, then a long sleep. Nothing else on the list.

slides.title: Plan riding days, not just kilometres

content.caption:
How do you plan a rest day on a multi-day bikepacking trip? Here is a simple way.

When: many riders plan one every 5–7 riding days, or after a hard stretch like a big climb or headwind. Pick a town with a shop, laundry and a bed.

How to use it: sleep first. Then laundry, resupply, a quick bike check (chain, brakes, tyres, bolts), and charge everything. Keep it light. A rest day is not a chore day.

Save this for your next trip plan.
